From: Dana Whitfield
To: Gabriel Fontes, Victor Alade
Subject: Question on Monthly Close Package – Line Item

Hi Gabriel and Victor,

I’m reviewing the monthly close package and need clarification on one line item. The figure for [specific line item] appears to be materially different from our prior month, and I want to make sure we’re not missing something before I sign off on the final numbers.

Could you provide the underlying detail or supporting entries for this line item? If there’s a timing difference or an adjustment that explains the variance, please note that as well. I need this before end of day Thursday so I can finalize the board deck.

Thanks,
Dana Whitfield
Controller, Kestrel Manufacturing

---

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Question on Monthly Close Package – Line Item

Hi Dana,

Thanks for flagging this — happy to clarify before Thursday.

The variance on that line item is primarily driven by a late vendor rebate credit of $18,432 that landed after the statements cut. Per our accrual policy, we rebooked it into June, which is why the figure moves materially versus prior month. This is documented in the close folder (segment note added, under 'June Close – Vendor Rebate Adjustment').

I’ve also attached a brief margin variance breakdown (volume, price, mix, cost) and the supporting entries. Quick summary for the board deck: volume decline is concentrated in Midwest regional distribution (~70%) and smaller accounts in Southeast/West Coast (~30%). Cost side is consistent with Victor's earlier context; no other timing differences beyond the rebate.

Let me know if you need anything else before you finalize. I’m available Thursday morning if you want to walk through it.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes

From: Gabriel Fontes
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Question on Monthly Close Package – Line Item

Hi Dana,

Happy to confirm the exact figures before Thursday.

The rebate credit that hit June is $18,432 in full — none of that amount was included in May's numbers. May closed with the original accrual estimate of $12,000 for this vendor program; when the actual credit came in at $18,432 after the June cut, we rebooked the delta of $6,432 into June, and the full $18,432 now sits in June as the corrected figure. So May's statements do not carry any portion of this credit.

I've added a revised P&L to the close folder (under 'June Close – Vendor Rebate Adjustment') with the rebate reclassified as a separate line so the underlying run-rate is clean for the board. The supporting entries and the original accrual documentation are also in that folder, alongside the margin variance breakdown we discussed.

Everything should be in place for your sign-off. I'll be available Thursday morning if anything else comes up, but no need to walk through unless you see something in the entries.

Best,
Gabriel Fontes

For the board deck, the underlying run-rate without the one-time credit is stable on the cost side; the operational trend you should highlight remains the volume decline in Midwest distribution (~70%) and smaller Southeast/West Coast accounts (~30%). Price and mix are essentially flat.

No need to walk through Thursday morning unless something else comes up — I'll keep an eye on my inbox if you have follow-ups while tying out the deck.

Best,

From: Victor Alade
To: Dana Whitfield
Subject: Re: Question on Monthly Close Package – Line Item

Dana,

Adding the cost-side context Gabriel referenced. Reconciliation ties out cleanly.

- Freight surcharges: ~$9,300 higher vs. May, driven by expedited lanes out of Midwest DCs.
- One-time material price adjustment: $4,150 credit from our primary steel vendor, booked in June per their revised invoice.
- Rebate credit: stable at $18,432 (as Gabriel confirmed — none in May).

No other timing differences on the cost side. The underlying run-rate is stable ex the one-time items.

Available Thursday if you need to walk through anything before signing off.

V
